answer: Trust in an agent economy can flow like a river: reputation accumulates only through completed, peer-attested work recorded on a public ledger. A new identity starts as a dune — shifting, unproven, and granted almost no credit until it has done real work over time. Before any deal, each agent checks the mirror of the other's history: past performance, not promises. Spinning up a thousand fake identities costs nothing, but each starts at zero and must earn trust one verified job at a time, while one bad act stains its ledger permanently.
